document.title: ABB Fusegear DIN-type HRC-fuse links, 2...1250 A
document.pages: Ordering table PDF p.10 (row OFAA2GG250 / 1SCA022701R0700); Technical data & Features PDF p.15; Dimension drawing PDF p.54 (printed p.52)

modelingNotes: Exact identity: ABB library ordering table lists OFAA2GG250 -> order code 1SCA022701R0700, NH size 2, 690 V/250 V, 250 A, power loss 20.6 W. This is the fuse LINK (replaceable element), not a fuse base (OFAX/OS) or a switch-disconnector (OS/OT).

Utilization category gG (general cable/line protection). Standards IEC 60269-1 & -2, DIN VDE 0636-1 & -2, DIN 43620-1 (technical-data page). Ceramic body, silver-plated copper knife-blade contacts, non-isolated gripping lugs.

Voltage capability is dual and bidirectional: 690 V AC and 250 V DC. It is deliberately NOT encoded as rating.nominal_voltage/voltage_type, because the compiler compares nominal_voltage exactly to circuit intent and this device is neither AC-only nor tied to one voltage. Rated current In = 250 A is recorded as terminal current capability; breaking capacity 80 kA (AC and DC) and 20.6 W loss are documentation only.

Two terminals '1' and '2' are the two knife-blade contacts (one at each end), confirmed on the visually inspected DIN dimension drawing. NH fuse links carry NO printed terminal numbering; '1'/'2' are functional aliases with no orientation/polarity meaning.

The single function 'element' is a normally-closed conducting path. A fuse must NOT be modeled as a permanent (fixed) link: it normally conducts but is a protective element, so no fixedLink joins the two nets.

No auxiliary contacts, no striker/microswitch terminal, no PE/bond point exist on the standard gG link. The blown-fuse indicator is visual only. Separately ordered OFM/OFS/OFD fuse monitors (aux contacts 11/14/21/22) are different parts and are not included here.
connectionCoverage is complete for the electrical interface (exactly two blades); only the (nonexistent) blade markings are unverified.

connectionCoverage.notes: The two knife-blade contacts are the complete electrical interface of the NH gG fuse link; no auxiliary, striker, or PE terminal exists. NH links carry no printed terminal designations, so '1'/'2' are functional aliases (unmarked), not verified markings.
